requirements.requirement: node1 /etc/inventory/app.conf exists and is treated as source of truth
requirements.summary: File did not exist initially; executor created it on node1 and used it as the origin for all subsequent sync verification. All later changes were made on node1 and observed to propagate to node2, consistent with node1 being the authoritative source.

requirements.requirement: A mechanism keeps node2's copy synchronized with node1's file, checking at an interval well under 15 minutes
requirements.summary: A root SSH keypair was provisioned for node2->node1 passwordless access, a pull-based sync script was installed on node2, and a root cron entry running the script every 5 minutes was installed and confirmed listed in crontab.

requirements.requirement: Initial content on node2 matches node1 after sync
requirements.summary: Manual first invocation of the sync script produced an identical copy on node2, verified by direct content comparison.

requirements.requirement: A real change to node1's app.conf is picked up on node2 within 15 minutes, via the automated (not manually-triggered) mechanism
requirements.summary: node1's file was modified, node2 was confirmed divergent immediately afterward, and cron log entries plus a subsequent content check show the scheduled (not manual) cron job applied the update autonomously roughly 1-4 minutes later, with matching md5sums on both nodes -- well within the 15-minute requirement.

requirements.requirement: Synchronization mechanism continues to function correctly after node restarts (regression coverage, though not an explicit task requirement)
requirements.summary: After both nodes were rebooted, a fresh change on node1 was again picked up autonomously by the cron-driven sync script on node2 (CROND log entry and matching md5sum), confirming the crontab and script persisted across reboot and the mechanism remains functional.

overall_summary: The executor established a working one-way pull sync (SSH + cron every 5 minutes) from node1's authoritative /etc/inventory/app.conf to node2, and directly demonstrated a real content change propagating autonomously via the scheduled cron job well within the 15-minute requirement, both before and after rebooting each node. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for both nodes with pre-restart baselines, acknowledged restarts, changed boot identities matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, and confirmed recovery of services, crontab, and file state.
limitations: Node local clock/timezone appears offset from the UTC command timestamps (cron log shows 'Sep 3 12:00:02' for a change issued at 2026-09-03T15:58:56Z); this does not affect the within-15-minute conclusion since the wall-clock gap between change and observed sync in executor timestamps was under 2 minutes, but absolute cron log timestamps should not be read as UTC.
Only two sync cycles (one pre-restart, one post-restart) were directly observed; longer-term reliability of the cron mechanism over many cycles was not captured.

One post-restart monitoring command (cmd-1be95de23ac44e91) failed due to a proxy timeout rather than a node-side issue; this did not affect the final propagation verification, which was completed by follow-up commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing executor commands (creating the source file, provisioning the SSH keypair/authorized_keys, installing the sync script and cron entry, the manual first sync, the two test edits to app.conf, and the two node reboots) have a clear, direct role in either satisfying the sync requirement or fulfilling the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol. No abandoned files, failed/conflicting services, unnecessary packages, or weakened security posture were introduced -- the after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no unexpected failed-services, listening-socket, or package-health deltas versus after_prepare beyond the expected boot-id/tmp-dir changes from the two reboots. The only minor note is that the two test/demonstration edits to app.conf ("changed_at=...", "post_restart_check=...") remain in the file as permanent content rather than being reverted after verification; since the executor itself created this file for the task, this is low-risk residue rather than unwanted mutation of pre-existing state.
